verdicts.detail: 2025-06-14 is the date the governor signed the law. It is not the date the law took effect. The cited session law (Laws 2025, 1st Sp. Sess. ch. 12) prints its own effective-date clause right after Sec. 9 [216B.1622]: 'This section is effective the day following final enactment.' The governor signed it on 14 June 2025, so by these words Sec. 9 took effect on 15 June 2025. The row's note keeps the reading group's wording ('signed; the section is effective the day following final enactment'), but the status date that was written down is the signing date.

The MPSC release does support Commission approval on 27 August 2026. But the approved rule is printed in DTE's rate book (the cached copy of great_lakes-04's source_url) on Second Revised Sheets C-4.00, C-5.00 and C-14.00 (PDF pp.45, 46 and 55), each 'Effective for service rendered on and after August 27, 2026' and issued 2 September 2026. Under the README, 'approved' means not yet in effect or no sheet yet. The row's own notes say the rule is in effect from that date. Because the rate book host allows personal use only, the cite would be an internal source; the row stays public through the MPSC release.

The value states the bespoke-resource reimbursement after commercial operation as unconditional. Sheet 272 (p.346) relieves the customer of further reimbursement if the Commission approves moving its share into the Company's rate base or assigning it to another customer. The WEC deck the value also cites says 'to the extent it cannot be repurposed'. The VLC parts are correct: continued pass-through charges or credits (p.313), and the undepreciated dedicated distribution facilities that can no longer serve another similar size customer (p.323).
verdicts.corrected_value: On early termination the customer stays responsible for certain pass-through charges (or receives certain credits); pays the remaining undepreciated book balance of dedicated distribution facilities that could no longer serve another similar size customer; for a bespoke resource terminated after commercial operation, reimburses the net book value of its share, but owes no further reimbursement if the Commission approves moving its share into the Company's rate base or assigning it directly to another customer (before commercial operation, its share of expenditures and cancellation fees not otherwise recoverable or mitigated)

verdicts.words: If the Commission approves moving the Customer's Share into the Company's rate base or assigning it directly to another customer under an applicable Company tariff, customer will not be obligated to reimburse the Company for any additional costs, including invested capital and accumulated AFUDC.
